en.title: State Minister Khaleel calls on Minister of Finance and Climate Change of Tuvalu
en.description: State Minister Khaleel calls on Minister of Finance and Climate Change of Tuvalu
en.body:
State Minister Khaleel calls on Minister of Finance and Climate Change of Tuvalu

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel has met with the Minister of Finance and Climate Change of Tuvalu, Seve Paeniu, this morning.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, State Minister Khaleel and Minister Paeniu discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation between the two countries. Both State Minister Khaleel and Minister Paeniu also reaffirmed their commitment to enhance collaboration at the multilateral fora and within the United Nations, to address global issues of mutual importance such as climate change and land adaptation.

Minister Paeniu was accompanied by Madam Malama Oilau Te’o-Paeniu, Spouse and Ms. Lafita Meatuai Paeniu, Senior Advisor for Pacific Divisions at the Department of Foreign Affairs of Tuvalu.State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Ms. Shiuneen Rasheed, Joint Secretary and Mr. Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Minister Paeniu is on an first official visit to Maldives from 17-22 November 2021, on the invitation of Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid. During his visit, Minister Paeniu will be making a courtesy call on His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives and will also meet with respective Cabinet Ministers in the Maldives.

en.title: New High Commissioner of India to Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
en.description: New High Commissioner of India to Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
en.body:
New High Commissioner of India to Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs

High Commissioner of India to Maldives, Munu Mahawar paid a courtesy call on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, today.

At the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, State Minister Khaleel congratulated the High Commissioner on presenting his credentials, and exchanged views over ways in which the positive dynamism in the Maldives-India relationship can be sustained and further strengthened.

Highlighting the various milestones achieved since His Excellency President Solih took office in November 2018, State Minister expressed appreciation of the people and the Government of Maldives to the Government of India for the support extended to Maldives in various fronts. State Minister also stressed on the generous assistance India provides to the Maldives throughout any crisis, including the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic.

High Commissioner Mahawar thanked for the warm welcome, and conveyed his commitment to working closely with the Government and people of the Maldives in continuing the efforts to enhance the bilateral relation between both countries in areas of mutual interest.

State Minister was accompanied by Joint Secretary, Abdul Waris Saeed and Director, Umaira Mohamed. High Commissioner was accompanied by Deputy High Commissioner Rohit Rathish.

en.title: Foreign Secretary Ghafoor participates at the 21st Council of Ministers of IORA
en.description: Foreign Secretary Ghafoor participates at the 21st Council of Ministers of IORA
en.body:
Foreign Secretary Ghafoor participates at the 21st Council of Ministers of IORA

Foreign Secretary, His Excellency Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed today participated in the 21st Meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA). The meeting was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh, under the theme “Harnessing the opportunities of the Indian Ocean sustainably for inclusive development”.

The meeting brought together Ministers from the Member States of IORA in which they reiterated their commitment to strengthening solidarity and enhancing multilateral cooperation to effectively respond to the challenges facing the Indian Ocean Region. The Dhaka Communiqué was adopted at the end of the meeting.

In his remarks, Foreign Secretary highlighted that IORA provides its Member States an interactive platform to deliberate and work together to achieve their shared perspective for a peaceful, stable and prosperous region. He noted that the unity and solidarity that IORA offers are impactful in shaping development plans of Small Island Developing States like the Maldives. He also urged Member States to steer their efforts to overcome the COVID-19 pandemic and to harness the resources of the Indian Ocean sustainably to recalibrate the approach to development, where no one is left behind. Further, he reiterated the firm commitment of the Maldives to the common principles enshrined in the IORA Charter and called on the Member States to revive the true spirit of regional cooperation.

IORA is a leading inter-governmental organization formed in 1997 to enhance regional and socio-economic cooperation and development within the Indian Ocean Region. The Maldives formally joined IORA on 8 November 2019, as its 22nd Member State.

en.title: New Non-Resident Ambassador of the Philippines to Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
en.description: New Non-Resident Ambassador of the Philippines to Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs

The newly appointed Non-Resident Ambassador of the Philippines to Maldives, His Excellency Alan L.Deniega called on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today, following the presentation of his credentials to H.E President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih at a ceremony held this morning at the President’s Office.

State Minister Khaleel congratulated Ambassador Deniega on his appointment as the Ambassador of the Philippines to Maldives and expressed hope that the close bilateral relations that exist between both the countries would be further strengthened during Ambassador Deniega’s tenure.

State Minister Khaleel thanked the Ambassador for the support the Phillippines continues to provide to the Maldives, especially during the pandemic and highlighted the important contributions made by Filipino workers in the Maldives, especially in the tourism and health sectors.

Ambassador Deniega also held meetings with senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Additional Secretary of the East and Central Asia Department, Mr. Javed Faizal, Executive Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ms.Fathmath Naeema and Desk Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mr.Ibrahim Haail.

en.title: State Minister hosts luncheon in honour of the visiting US Assistant Secretary of State
en.description: State Minister hosts luncheon in honour of the visiting US Assistant Secretary of State
en.body:
State Minister hosts luncheon in honour of the visiting US Assistant Secretary of State

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel hosts a luncheon in honour of the visiting Assistant Secretary of State for the Bureau of South and Central Asian Affairs of the United States Department of State, Donald Lu, today.

During this luncheon, State Minister Khaleel and Assistant Secretary of State Lu discussed the traditionally close bilateral relationship between the Maldives and the United States including existing bilateral cooperation programmes and global matters of mutual importance. The discussions also focsed on the establishment of a resident US Embassy, as well as expanding cooperation in the fields of education, environment and climate change, economic cooperation, cybersecurity, good governance, and countering terrorism and preventing violent extremism.

State Minister Khaleel and Assistant Secretary of State Lu further reiterated the commitment of both countries to working together to fortify the existing bond between the Maldives and the United States of America.

Assistant Secretary of State Lu was accompanied by Chargé d'affaires at the Embassy of the United States of America, Mr. Martin Kelly, Executive Director at the Bureau of South and Central Asian Affairs of the Department of State of the United States of America, Ms. Rachna Korhonen, and senior officials from the United States Department of State and the Embassy of the United States of America.

State Minister Ahmed Khaleel was accompanied by Chief of Protocol, Ms. Aishath Shaan Shakir, Additional Secretary, Mr. Ahmed Shiaan, Joint Secretary, Ms. Shiuneen Rasheed, and senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives.

Assistant Secretary Lu is currently on a two day official visit to the Maldives.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid delivers statement at the virtual COVID-19 ministerial hosted by the United States Secretary of State
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid delivers statement at the virtual COVID-19 ministerial hosted by the United States Secretary of State
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid delivers statement at the virtual COVID-19 ministerial hosted by the United States Secretary of State

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid today delivered a statement at the virtual COVID-19 ministerial hosted by the United States Secretary of State Antony Blinken. In his statement, Minister Shahid highlighted the challenging circumstances presented by the COVID-19 pandemic across the globe, and the need for a consolidated global effort to address such catastrophes.

In his speech, Minister Shahid highlighted the vital role played by the Government of the United States in supporting the Government of Maldives’ efforts to combat the virus, including multiple donations of Personal Protective Equipment, ventilators and vaccines that have increased the capacity of the Maldives to combat the spread of the virus more effectively. He also commended the United States leadership in coordinating a global response in addressing the pandemic.

Minister Shahid also welcomed the Government of the United States decision to support the establishment of the Global Health Threats Council and noted the vital role played by multilateral initiatives such as COVAX and GAVI in streamlining a global response to future health security threats. He further called the member states to renew their vow to increase cooperation amongst the members in order to ensure success of global mechanisms and prevent, detect and respond to future health security threats effectively.

The virtual COVID-19 ministerial hosted by the United States Secretary of State was focused on recognizing the leading role of foreign ministers in identifying solutions and gaps to ending the pandemic and building better health security to prevent and respond to future infectious disease and other biological threats.

en.title: Minister Shahid participates in the National Scout Youth Symposium
en.description: Minister Shahid participates in the National Scout Youth Symposium
en.body:
Minister Shahid participates in the National Scout Youth Symposium

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, today delivered remarks at the National Scout Youth Symposium organized by the Scout Association of Maldives and the National Scout Youth Council.

In his remarks, Minister Shahid acknowledged young people’s contribution to our national development journey, from a low-income country to an upper-middle-income country and urged to ensure that policies and actions are targeted at leaving no one behind and reaching the furthest behind first in order to create a tolerant, compassionate and cohesive society. Minister Shahid then emphasized that youth must be empowered by involving them in decision making processes and providing them with the opportunity to have a say in shaping the future they deserve.

Minister Shahid also applauded the Scout Association of Maldives and the National Scout Youth Council for their contribution towards building a strong and promising youth population for a bright future for the Maldives.

en.title: Message from His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, on the occasion of UN Day
en.description: Message from His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, on the occasion of UN Day
en.body:
Message from His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, on the occasion of UN Day

“Today, as we celebrate the seventy-sixth anniversary of the United Nations, we reaffirm our trust in multilateralism and diplomacy, while celebrating the achievements of the Maldives in the UN.

Guided by the principles enshrined in the UN Charter, we move forward, together with all Member States, by demonstrating leadership and commitment to upholding the spirit of multilateralism, as it is key to addressing global challenges, including the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, climate change, terrorism and extremism, among others.

With the hope of a better future for all, the Maldives’ commitment to the UN remains steadfast, and we will continue to promote human rights, democracy, justice and equality for all nations alike, big or small, rich or poor. The deepening of inequalities among vulnerable groups within the society as a result of the devastating impacts of COVID-19 is undeniable.

The Maldives joined the United Nations in 1965, one of the first small states to join the organization, and a least developed country at the time. Despite its size, the Maldives has been an active member of the UN since then and the trust placed by the international community in the Maldives is evident by the election of the Maldives’ candidate to the seventy sixth session of the UN General Assembly. As the candidate of the Maldives, it is a great honour and privilege for me to serve as the current President of the UN General Assembly. I assure all Member States that this is a presidency of hope for people, the planet and prosperity, where no one is left behind. Together we can achieve the sustainable development goals and its Agenda 2030 and together we shall reach the target set forth in the Paris Agreement, in global solidarity and in the spirit of multilateralism, these challenges could be overcome to provide a better future for generation to come.”

en.title: MoUs signed between the Maldives and India to implement eight projects under High Impact Community Development scheme
en.description: MoUs signed between the Maldives and India to implement eight projects under High Impact Community Development scheme
en.body:
MoUs signed between the Maldives and India to implement eight projects under High Impact Community Development scheme

The signing ceremony of eight Memorandum of Understandings between the Government of Maldives and Government of India has been held today at Ministry of Foreign Affairs. These MoUs will be implemented under Indian grant assistance scheme for High Impact Community Development Project (HICDP) through local bodies.

The Ceremony was attended by members of Parliament, senior officials from the Government of Maldives and the High Commission of India.

In his remarks delivered at the ceremony, Foreign Minister Shahid highlighted that the projects launched under the MoUs will contribute significantly to socio-economic development, livelihood activity, conservation of environmental and cultural heritage, empowerment of women and child welfare and skills development. Minister Shahid also emphasized the continued support and assistance in various forms received from the Government of India for the socio-economic development of Maldives.

The projects launched under the MoUs signed today are worth a total grant of 36,609,600 Rufiya (equivalent to USD 2,374,163). The projects include the acquisition of two sea ambulances; strengthening inclusive education support units in three schools, in G.Dh. Thinadhoo, L. Gan and HA. Dhidhdhoo; development of an ice plant in L. Maabaidhoo; Olympus hall upgrading project; construction of a multi-purpose council building in N. Miladhoo; construction of Dhangethi Cultural Centre and installation of street lights in Th. Thimarafushi and Th. Veymandoo.

The MoUs were signed by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel on behalf of the Government of Maldives and the High Commissioner of India, His Excellency Sunjay Sudhir, on behalf of the Government of India.

The overarching Memorandum of Understanding on Indian Grant Assistance for Implementation of High Impact Community Development Projects through local bodies, was initially signed between the Governments of the Maldives and India on 17 March 2019 for grant of 85 million Rufiya and renewed with an increment up to 155 million Rufiya (equivalent to approximately US$10 million), on 23 July 2021.

Apart from the projects launched today, twelve projects are currently underway, under this grant scheme. They include the establishment of Geydhoshu Mas Plant (Neighbourhood Fish Processing Plants) in Hithadhoo, Maradhoo and Hulhudhoo of Addu City, and Noonu Kendhikulhudhoo; Development of tourism zones in Hithadhoo, Feydhoo, Maradhoo, Meedhoo and Hulhudhoo of Addu City; Agricultural Linkages Project in Hanimaadhoo by the Ministry of Fisheries, Agriculture and Marine Resources; Establishing a drug detox centre in Addu City Hulhudhoo; Establishing a Water Bottling Factory in Haa Alif Hoarafushi.

dv.title: އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގައި 8 މަޝްރޫއެއް ހިންގުމަށް ސޮއިކޮށްފި
dv.description: އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގައި 8 މަޝްރޫއެއް ހިންގުމަށް ސޮއިކޮށްފި
dv.body:
އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގައި 8 މަޝްރޫއެއް ހިންގުމަށް ސޮއިކޮށްފި

އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގެ ދަށުން 8 މަޝްރޫއެއް ހިންގުމަށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރާ ދެމެދު އެމް.އޯ.ޔޫގައި މިއަދު ސޮއިކޮށްފިއެވެ. މި އެމް.އޯ.ޔޫތަކަކީ އިންޑިއާގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގެ ދަށުން ހައި އިމްޕެކްޓް ކޮމިއުނިޓީ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް (އެޗް.އައި.ސީ.ޑީ.ޕީ) ގެ ދަށުން އެކި އިދާރާތައް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ހިންގުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ މަޝްރޫތަކެވެ.

އެމް.އޯ.ޔޫގައި ސޮއިކުރުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ ބައެއް މެންބަރުންނާއި، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި އިންޑިއާ ހައިކޮމިޝަންގެ އިސް ބޭފުޅުން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގެންނެވިއެވެ.

މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވީޑިއޯ ކޮންފަރެންސް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ވާހަކަފުޅުދައްކަވަމުން ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދު ވަނީ މި އެމް.އޯ.ޔޫތަކުގެ ދަށުން އިފްތިތާޙްކުރެވޭ މަޝްރޫޢުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން އިޖްތިމާޢީ އަދި އިޤްތިޞާދީ ތަރައްޤީއާއި، ތިމާވެއްޓާއި ޘަޤާފީ ތަރިކަ ރައްކާތެރިކުރުމާއި، އަންހެނުން ބާރުވެރިކުރުވުމާއި، ކުޑަކުދިންގެ ދުޅަހެޔޮކަމާއި އަދި ހުނަރު ތަރައްޤީކުރުމަށް ބޮޑު އެހީތެރިކަމެއް ލިބިގެންދާނެކަން ފާހަގަކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި ރާއްޖޭގެ އިޖްތިމާއީ އަދި އިގްތިސާދީ ތަރައްގީއަށް އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުން އެކި ގޮތްގޮތުން ވެދެއްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ އެހީތެރިކަމާއި އެއްބާރުލެއްވުން މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

މިއަދު ސޮއިކުރި އެމްއޯޔޫތަކުގެ ދަށުން އިފްތިތާހުކުރި މަޝްރޫއުތަކަކީ ޖުމްލަ 36،609،600 ރުފިޔާ (2،374،163 ޑޮލަރު) ގެ ހިލޭ އެހީ އެކެވެ. މި މަޝްރޫޢުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި، 2 ސީ އެމްބިއުލާންސް ހޯދުމާއި، ގދ.ތިނަދޫ، ލ.ގަން އަދި ހއ.ދިއްދޫ ގެ ސްކޫލުތަކުގެ އިންކްލޫސިވް އެޑިޔުކޭޝަން ސަޕޯޓް ޔުނިޓް ހަރުދަނާކުރުން، ލ.މާބައިދޫގައި އައިސް ޕްލާންޓެއް ތަރައްޤީކުރުން، އޮލިމްޕަސް ހޯލް އަޕްގްރޭޑިން ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް، ނ. މިލަދޫގައި މަލްޓި ޕާޕަސް ކައުންސިލް އިމާރާތެއް އިމާރާތްކުރުން، އދ. ދަނގެތީ ކަލްޗަރަލް ސެންޓަރު އިމާރާތްކުރުމާއި ތ. ތިމަރަފުއްޓާއި ތ. ވޭމަންޑޫގެ މަގުބައްތި ހަރުކުރުން ހިމެނެއެވެ.

މި އެމްއޯޔޫތަކުގައި ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ސޮއިކުރެއްވީ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ސްޓޭޓް ފޮރ ފޮރިން އެފެއަރޒް އަޙްމަދު ޚަލީލެވެ. އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ސޮއިކުރެއްވީ އިންޑިއާއިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު ސަންޖޭ ސުދީރުއެވެ. 85 މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ ހިލޭ އެހީގެ މި ސްކީމްގައި އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާ ދެމެދު އެމްއޯޔޫއެއްގައި ފުރަތަމަ ސޮއިކޮށްފައިވަނީ 17 މާޗް 2019 ގައެވެ. އަދި މި ސްކީމް 155 މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާއަށް އިތުރުކުރުމަށް ސޮއިކޮށްފައިވަނީ 23 ޖުލައި 2021 ގައެވެ.

މިއަދު އިފްތިތާޙު ކުރެވުނު މަޝްރޫޢުތަކުގެ އިތުރުން، މި ގްރާންޓް ސްކީމްގެ ދަށުން މިހާރުވެސް 12 މަޝްރޫޢެއްގެ މަސައްކަތް ހިނގަމުން އެބަދޭ. އެގޮތުން އައްޑޫ ސިޓީ ހިތަދޫ، މަރަދޫ އަދި ހުޅުދޫ އަދި ނ. ނެދިކުޅުދޫގައި ގޭދޮށު މަސް ޕްލާންޓް ގާއިމުކުރުމާއި، އައްޑޫ ސިޓީ ހިތަދޫ، ފޭދޫ، މަރަދޫ، މީދޫ އަދި ހުޅުދޫގައި ޓޫރިޒަމް ޒޯންތައް ތަރައްގީކުރުމާއި، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފިޝަރީޒް، އެގްރިކަލްޗަރ އެންޑް މެރިން ރިސޯސަސްގެ ފަރާތުން ހަނިމާދޫގައި ހިންގާ އެގްރިކަލްޗަރަލް ލިންކޭޖްސް ޕްރޮޖެކްޓާއި، އައްޑޫ ސިޓީ ހުޅުދޫގައި ޑްރަގް ޑީޓޮކްސް ސެންޓަރެއް ގާއިމުކުރުމާއި ހއ.ހޯރަފުށީގައި ވޯޓަރ ބޮޓްލިންގ ފެކްޓްރީއެއް ޤާއިމުކުރުމުގެ މަސައްކަތް ކުރިއަށްދެއެވެ.

en.title: US Ambassador pays a farewell call on State Minister
en.description: US Ambassador pays a farewell call on State Minister
en.body:
US Ambassador pays a farewell call on State Minister

The Ambassador of United States of America to the Republic of Maldives Alaina Teplitz paid a farewell call on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, today.

State Minister Khaleel congratulated the Ambassador on the completion of her successful tenure and thanked her for her role in reinvigorating the close and cordial ties between the United States and the Maldives and for the enhanced cooperation between the two countries. The State Minister also thanked the Ambassador for the generous support extended to the Maldives during her ambassadorial tenure. Ambassador Teplitz conveyed her gratitude to the Government and the people of Maldives for the continuous support and hospitality accorded to her.

Discussions were also held on the existing bilateral relations, and explored on expanding the cooperation between the two countries especially in the field of climate change, security, trade and investments and as well as cooperation at the multilateral fora.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Shiuneen Rasheed, Joint Secretary and Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.title: State Minister Khaleel meets with Australian Minister for Trade, Tourism and Investment
en.description: State Minister Khaleel meets with Australian Minister for Trade, Tourism and Investment
en.body:
State Minister Khaleel meets with Australian Minister for Trade, Tourism and Investment

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, has met with the Minister for Trade, Tourism and Investment of Australia Dan Tehan, this morning.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, both State Minister and Australian Trade Minister held discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two countries in areas such as economic and trade cooperation, education, people to people contact and environment and climate change.

State Minister Khaleel also expressed appreciation for the multiple contributions made by the Australian Government that played a key role in the Government’s efforts to controlling the COVID-19 outbreak within the country. Both State Minister and Australian Trade Minister also reassured commitment towards working closely on furthering collaborations on the multilateral front.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Shiuneen Rasheed, Joint Secretary, Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim, Assistant Director and Hussain Azhaan Mohamed Hussain, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.title: Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Norway presents credentials to the King of Norway
en.description: Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Norway presents credentials to the King of Norway
en.body:
Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Norway presents credentials to the King of Norway

Ambassador of Maldives to the Federal Republic of Germany, His Excellency Ahmed Latheef presented his Letters of Credence to His Majesty King Harald V, King of Norway as the Non-Resident Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Maldives to Norway at a ceremony held at the Royal Palace in Oslo today.

During the Credential Ceremony, Ambassador Latheef conveyed greetings from His Excellency President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of Maldives to the President and the people of Norway. Ambassador Latheef further expressed commitment to work closely with the Norwegian Government to enhance the bilateral relationship between both countries.

During his visit to Norway, Ambassador Latheef met with Director Mr. Mattis Raustøl, and Senior Adviser Ms. Anne Glad Fredriksen, at the Section for South Asia and Afghanistan and Mr. Torgeir Larsen, Deputy Secretary General at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Norway and discussed on further strengthening the bilateral and multilateral cooperation between the two countries. Ambassador Latheef also paid a call on Her Excellency Maw Maw, Ambassador of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar and Dean of the Diplomatic Corps in Oslo.

Ambassador Latheef also met with Ms. Helga Cotgrove, CFO and Mr. Filippo Comelli, EVP for Project Finance & and project Development of Norsk Solar and discussed with them about expansion of renewable energy projects in the Maldives. He also had a meeting with Mr. Gunnar Stølsvik, Specialist Director at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries of Norway and discussed projects being implemented under the Blue Justice Initiative.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Equatorial Guinea
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Equatorial Guinea
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Equatorial Guinea

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends message of felicitations to Simeón Oyono Esono Angué, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Equatorial Guinea, on the occasion of the Independence Day of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“Let me extend warm greetings and sincere well wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the friendly people of Equatorial Guinea, on the occasion of your Independence Day.

It is my earnest wish that the close friendship between our two countries will continue to grow stronger in the years ahead. Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Minister for Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation of Spain
en.description: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Minister for Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation of Spain
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Minister for Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation of Spain

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sent a message of felicitations to José Manuel Albares Bueno, Minister for Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation of Spain, on the occasion of the National Day of Spain.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to convey warm greetings and sincere good wishes of the Government and the people of Maldives, and those of my own, to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Spain, on the joyous occasion of the National Day of Spain.

en.title: State Minister Khaleel delivers statement at the High-Level Commemorative Meeting to mark the 60th Anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
en.description: State Minister Khaleel delivers statement at the High-Level Commemorative Meeting to mark the 60th Anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
en.body:
State Minister Khaleel delivers statement at the High-Level Commemorative Meeting to mark the 60th Anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel today delivered a statement at the ongoing High-Level Commemorative Meeting to mark the 60th Anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), which is being held in Belgrade, Serbia. In his statement, State Minister noted that despite its diversity NAM stands tall and united behind its common founding vision and has proven to be a formidable player in shaping world politics since its inception. This commemorative meeting is one of the many markers of the strength of our Movement, he said.

The State Minister underlined the relevance of the Bandung Principles as time-tested and stressed the importance to continue to respect and uphold them as they come under increasing pressure. State Minister reiterated that Maldives takes great pride in being a member of the movement and will remain firmly committed to continuing to be an active member. He urged the member states to work together, peacefully, while recognising and respecting the differences among the members. He further called the member states to renew its vow to increase cooperation amongst the members and also with others through various multilateral avenues. While highlighting the impacts of COVID-19 he called the member states to work together with renewed motivation to recover from the unprecedented COVID-19 pandemic. He further stated that it is more vital than ever to embrace multilateralism and not retreat to isolationism and NAM must play a central role in this effort.

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs is being accompanied to the Commemorative Meeting by Her Excellency Thilmeeza Hussain, Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations, His Excellency Ahmed Shiaan, Additional Secretary and Ms. Fathimath Naeema, Executive Director of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The NAM comprises of 120 Member States, and is one of the largest international organizations after the United Nations. The Maldives became a member of NAM in 1976.

en.title: India lifts travel restrictions and resume visa-free travel to India for Maldivian nationals
en.description: India lifts travel restrictions and resume visa-free travel to India for Maldivian nationals
en.body:
India lifts travel restrictions and resume visa-free travel to India for Maldivian nationals

The Government of India lifts the COVID-19 restrictions to travel to India for Maldivians who wishes to travel to India for medical, business and tourism purposes effective from 15 October 2021.

The decision will fully restore the Visa Facilitation Agreement signed between Maldives and India during the State Visit by His Excellency President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih to India in December 2018, to facilitate easier travel between both countries.

Maldives is the first beneficiary of visa-free travel since COVID-19 travel restrictions were imposed by India in March 2020. India has been among the first to respond during this pandemic, as it has with every crisis Maldives has faced, through the many gestures of goodwill, humanitarian assistance, and friendship.

en.title: Statement by the Government of Maldives on the hostile attack on King Abdullah Airport in Jazan, Kingdom of Saudi ArabiA
en.description: Statement by the Government of Maldives on the hostile attack on King Abdullah Airport in Jazan, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
en.body:
Statement by the Government of Maldives on the hostile attack on King Abdullah Airport in Jazan, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

The Government of Maldives strongly condemns the hostile attack on King Abdullah Airport in Jazan, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with the use of bomb-laden drone on 08 October 2021.

The continuation of such deliberate attacks targeting vital civilian infrastructure undoubtedly violates the international laws, and the resulting civilian casualties clearly exhibits the elevated threat to the stability of the region. Such deplorable acts of terrorism indicate the urgent need for constructive engagement by the parties concerned to find peaceful solutions to the conflicts.

The Government of Maldives reaffirms its solidarity with the brotherly people and the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and reiterates its steadfast commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.

en.title: Japan Gives a Grant Aid of 400 Million Japanese Yen for the Provision of a Sea Ambulance
en.description: Japan Gives a Grant Aid of 400 Million Japanese Yen for the Provision of a Sea Ambulance
en.body:
Japan Gives a Grant Aid of 400 Million Japanese Yen for the Provision of a Sea Ambulance

The Government of Japan has provided a grant aid of 400 Million Japanese Yen (approximately 3 million USD) to the Maldives to promote economic and social development in the country. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel and the Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives, Her Excellency Keiko Yanai signed the Exchange of Notes relating to the grant aid, at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today.

This grant aid will be utilised to further strengthen the capacities of the health service providers in the country. This includes the provision of a sea ambulance equipped with the necessary medical systems and trained staff to be used in the event of a serious illness or medical condition, and on emergency evacuations.

While speaking at the ceremony State Minister Khaleel highlighted that the demand for Sea Ambulance services has increased immensely, especially due to the ongoing global pandemic and the health sector is constantly struggling to match its resources and capabilities. This assistance extended by the Government of Japan is a much needed and timely boost to the capabilities of the sea ambulance service and will ensure reliable and uninterrupted service for emergency transfer or medical evacuation of patients during rough weather conditions.

State Minister Khaleel thanked the Government of Japan for the grant aid, characterising it as yet another important gesture of Japan’s goodwill and extraordinary generosity to the Maldives. The signing ceremony was attended by senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Defence and National Security, Ministry of Health and the officials from the Embassy of Japan.

en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs delivers a video message at the virtual reception to mark the 72nd Anniversary of the Founding of the People’s Republic of China.

Minister Abdulla Shahid has delivered a video message at the virtual reception held today by the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China to mark the 72nd Anniversary of the Founding of the People’s Republic of China and the assumption of Office by H.E Ambassador Wang Lixin on 6 September 2021.

In his message, Minister Shahid extended greetings and good wishes to H.E. Xi Jinping, President, the Government and the friendly people of China from President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of Maldives. Minister Shahid also congratulated Ambassador Wang Lixin on assuming her post as the new Ambassador of China to the Maldives.

Minister Shahid’s message stated that the bilateral relationship between Maldives and China are founded on the Maldives commitment to the One China Policy, and our shared values and principles of equality and mutual respect. Minister expressed his gratitude for the support extended by the Government of China to the Maldives during the most challenging times of COVID-19 pandemic, by donating vaccines and other medical equipment to Maldives efforts to curb the virus. Minister reiterated that Maldives will continue to work with China in the international arena on issues of mutual interest and looks forward to further strengthening the bilateral relationship that exist between two countries.

Minister concluded his message by stating that he looks forward to working closely with Ambassador Wang Lixin and he is confident that both countries can reach new heights in the China-Maldives bilateral relationship.

The reception was attended by the Foreign Secretary, H.E Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, Secretary Multilateral, H.E. Dr Hala Hameed, Additional Secretary Javed Faizal and Senior Officials at the Ministry.

Foreign Minister Shahid’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to congratulate and extend my best wishes to you, the Government and the friendly people of the Russian Federation on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between our two countries.

During the past fifty-five years of close cordial relations, both our countries have developed an exemplary bond of friendship founded on shared values, mutual understanding and goodwill. The Government of Maldives is grateful for the many contributions Russia has made towards the socio-economic development in the Maldives, particularly in the field of tourism. Tourism is the largest economic industry of the Maldives and Russia has always been a key tourism market, currently holding the top position of the tourist arrivals in the country. It is our hope that the cooperation on this front would be strengthened in the future, along with existing trade relations between both our countries. I look forward to working together with renewed impetus to further enhance our cooperation and collaboration both bilaterally and in the multilateral fora.

Let me extend my best wishes and prayers for your success, good health and well-being, and the continued progress and welfare of the people of the Russian Federation.”

Foreign Minister Lavrov’s message reads as follows:

The Russian-Maldivian relations are based on the principles of equality and mutual respect. We note the substantial nature of the bilateral political dialogue, the intensity of which has significantly risen in recent years. en.title: Second Senior Officials Meeting between the EU and the Maldives confirms commitment to strengthen relations
en.description: Second Senior Officials Meeting between the EU and the Maldives confirms commitment to strengthen relations
en.body:
Second Senior Officials Meeting between the EU and the Maldives confirms commitment to strengthen relations

The second Senior Officials Meeting between the European Union and the Maldives was held on 10 September 2021 in Brussels. The Senior Officials Meeting was established in June 2019 with the objective of enhancing cooperation between the EU and the Maldives through yearly exchanges.

The EU and the Maldives welcomed the very positive momentum in the relations, as highlighted by a large and growing bilateral agenda, and reaffirmed their willingness to further strengthen the relationship between the people of the EU and the Maldives, including working together in the context of the EU Strategy on Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. As a strong signal of this commitment, the EU and the Maldives welcomed the 19 April 2021 Council decision to launch the negotiations on an EU - Maldives Partnership and Cooperation Agreement, and agreed on the next steps in advancing these negotiations.

The European Union and the Maldives recalled the significant steps taken over the last year to enhance and deepen cooperation in a number of areas of strategic importance for both, notably green recovery, climate change, good governance, judicial reform and security. The Maldives also thanked the EU for its timely assistance following the outbreak of COVID-19, through a EUR 3 million grant to strengthen the health sector and assist in economic recovery efforts. The EU stressed its commitment to provide continuous support for actions in these priority areas and announced that a bilateral financial allocation for the Maldives will be made available as part of the Multi-annual Indicative Programme for the coming four years, to support the above aims.

With regard to security, the Maldives updated the European Union on progress in the investigation of the 6 May attack on Speaker Mohamed Nasheed and noted that the EU support for counter-terrorism activities in the Maldives has been particularly pertinent in this context. The EU stressed that supporting the Maldives in combatting terrorism and violent extremism is among its priorities. The EU and the Maldives agreed to explore additional opportunities to cooperate on enhancing counter-terrorism measures and countering violent extremism in the future.

The EU has expressed its appreciation for the commitment reiterated by the Government of the Maldives towards consolidating democracy, upholding and promoting human rights, strengthening the rule of law and fighting corruption. The EU welcomed the progress made in preparing the new judicial reform and anti-corruption efforts. The two sides also noted that the recent signature of the Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance on Tax Matters was an important step in tax good governance. The EU also stressed that a fully empowered and resilient civil society, in all its diversity, is a crucial component of any democracy. The EU expressed its continued readiness to support the Maldives in these efforts.

Both the European Union and the Maldives confirmed that stepping up cooperation on global challenges such as climate change and environment is among their top priorities. It was agreed that recovery from the global COVID-19 crisis should be used as a chance to rebuild the economies in a sustainable manner. The EU informed of its recent actions to enhance its climate ambition, including climate neutrality by 2050 and the increased 2030 targets of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% compared to 1990. The EU also noted the significance of its recently launched Blue Economy Agenda. The Maldives confirmed its commitment to taking ambitious action to ensure a sustainable, low-carbon and climate resilient development and emphasized the need for scaled up climate financing to achieve this development. The EU and the Maldives agreed on the importance of the environment in all fora and noted in particular that the upcoming UN conferences – the 26th session of the Conference of the Parties (COP 26) to the UNFCCC, the 15th Conference of the Parties on Biodiversity and the launching of negotiations for a global agreement on plastic at the UN Environmental Assembly in February 2022, and the Second UN Ocean Conference to be held in Lisbon, Portugal in 2022 - will present vital opportunities for the international community to make ambitious, meaningful commitments. It was agreed to cooperate closely to advance the climate change agenda in both bilateral and multilateral settings.

The EU and the Maldives also discussed on cooperation in the area of fishery, with particular regard to the sustainable management of fish stocks in the Indian Ocean through the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission and combatting IUU fishing in the region. The EU expressed its willingness to have a new session of the dialogue on IUU fishing by the end of this year. The EU congratulated the Maldives once again on the election of Foreign Minister Shahid as the 76th President of the UN General Assembly. The EU and the Maldives agreed to expand their partnership in the multilateral domain and work closely together on a number of mutual priorities in the UN.

The EU and the Maldives concurred on the importance of working to further enhance trade relations and agreed to continue to facilitate trade and investment. The Government of the Maldives reiterated its request to the EU to consider granting duty free access for sustainably sourced tuna products from the Maldives. At the Meeting, the Government of Maldives also reiterated its request for visa free travel for Maldivian nationals to travel to EU Member States with the view of strengthening existing ties between the Maldives and the EU.

The discussions were co-chaired by Ms Paola Pampaloni, Deputy Managing Director for Asia and Pacific at the European External Action Service and Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, Foreign Secretary of the Republic of Maldives.

en.title: Foreign Secretary Ghafoor holds bilateral engagements with the European Union, and Belgium
en.description: Foreign Secretary Ghafoor holds bilateral engagements with the European Union, and Belgium
en.body:
Foreign Secretary Ghafoor holds bilateral engagements with the European Union, and Belgium

Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed held bilateral engagements, today, with senior officials from the European Union and Belgium Government.

The Foreign Secretary held a meeting this morning with the Director in Charge of Directorate C at Directorate-General for Trade Ms. Ewa Synowiec and discussed avenues for further strengthening trade cooperation between the Maldives and the European Union. Further discussions were held regarding elimination of tariff on Maldivian tuna exports to the European Union.

Foreign Secretary Ghafoor also met with Head of Unit at Directorate-General for International Partnerships, Mr. Mario Ronconi, and discussed enhancing the Maldives-European Union partnership and explored the avenues for increasing investment from the European Union, in the Maldives. Foreign Secretary Ghafoor and Head of Unit Ronconi also discussed future cooperation between the Maldives and the European Union in economic and social development.

The Foreign Secretary held a meeting this afternoon with Director General of Directorate-General of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, Ms. Charlina Vitcheva and discussed enhancing cooperation between the Maldives and the European Union in conserving marine resources and the oceans. Further discussions included cooperation at the multilateral fora in areas of mutual concern regarding marine resources, fisheries and the oceans.

Foreign Secretary Ghafoor met with Deputy Secretary General of European External Action Service, Ms. Helena König, at the European External Action Service Office, and discussed avenues for strengthening cooperation between the Maldives and the European Union in areas such as trade, economic development, and tourism cooperation.

Discussions also included obtaining free Schengen visa for Maldivians and starting negotiations for a Partnership and Cooperation Agreement between the Maldives and the European Union.

Foreign Secretary Ghafoor met the Acting Director General for Bilateral Affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Belgium, Mr. Jeroen Cooreman, this evening, and discussed the avenues for enhancing the bilateral ties between the Maldives and Belgium and discussed cooperation at various fora in issues of mutual concern for the Maldives and Belgium.

Foreign Secretary Ghafoor was accompanied by Secretary, Multilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Ambassador of the Maldives to Belgium and the European Union, Hassan Sobir, Deputy Minister of Economic Development Riyaz Mansoor, Joint Secretary, Shiuneen Rasheed, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Hussain Azhaan Mohamed Hussain, and Assistant Director at the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology, Mariyam Anaa Hassan.

Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed is visiting Belgium to co-chair the Second Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union. The Maldives delegation participating in this meeting includes senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the President's Office, Maldives Police Service, Ministry of Economic Development, National Counter Terrorism Centre, and Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology. The Second Senior Officials Meeting will be held on 10 September 2021 in Brussels, Belgium.

en.title: Foreign Secretary attends the inauguration of the EP-Maldives Friendship Group
en.description: Foreign Secretary attends the inauguration of the EP-Maldives Friendship Group
en.body:
Foreign Secretary attends the inauguration of the EP-Maldives Friendship Group

Today, 14 Members of the European Parliament from the political groups of EPP, S&D, Renew, ECR and ID, representing 11 different nationalities founded the “EP-Maldives Friendship Group” at the European Parliament.

The EP-Maldives Friendship Group will serve as a platform for regular exchanges of views and discussions between Members of the European Parliament and Maldivian representatives. The main objective of the informal group is to contribute to fostering closer ties with the European Union and building new avenues of cooperation in the coming years.

During the inaugural meeting, members of the EP-Maldives Friendship Group warmly welcomed the Foreign Secretary, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed and the rest of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs delegation of senior officials who have travelled to Brussels to participate in the 2nd Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union.

In his opening remarks, the Chairman of the Group, MEP Tomáš Zdechovský said: “The diplomatic relations of Maldives and the EU has just entered a new phase. From now on, Maldivians can count on the support of our European Parliament Friendship Group and know that the deepening of the EU-Maldives cooperation will remain on the European Parliament table”.

Foreign Secretary, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, noted that “The launching of the Friendship Group of Maldives within the European Parliament is a key moment in the history of our relations and renews our commitment to continue the path towards fully consolidating democracy, ensuring good governance and promoting respect for human rights”.

“I am thankful to Tomáš Zdechovský MEP for yet another initiative to help the people of the Maldives. A permanent Friendship Group in the European Parliament will facilitate the exchange of information and discussion about the developments in our country. We know that we can count on the support of Tomáš Zdechovský and other Members of the Group for making Maldives an important partner of EU”, added Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed.

During the meeting with the Members of the European Parliament, Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed briefed the EP-Maldives Friendship Group on the current situation in the country, as well as on the recent developments in the Maldives-European Union relations.

en.title: Maldives delegation departs for 2nd Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union
en.description: Maldives delegation departs for 2nd Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union
en.body:
Maldives delegation departs for 2nd Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union

The Maldives delegation attending the Second Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union departs to Brussel, Belgium, tonight.

The Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union is held annually to facilitate open and constructive engagement between the Maldives and the European Union and to further strengthen the existing ties of friendship and cooperation between the Maldives and the European Union. This is the second iteration of this meeting, and will be held in Brussels, Belgium on 10 September 2021. The First Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union was held in February 2020.

The thematic areas of discussion at this year’s meeting will be on Governance, Democracy, Human rights, Rule of Law; Prevention of Violent Extremism and Counter-Terrorism; Economic and Trade Cooperation; Development Cooperation including ‘economic recovery and resilience’; sectoral issues; regional cooperation; and international cooperation.

The Maldives delegation will be led by Foreign Secretary, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed. Senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the President’s Office, Maldives Police Service, Ministry of Economic Development, National Counter Terrorism Centre, and Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology will also be in attendance.

The delegation from the European Union will be led by the Deputy Managing Director at the European External Action Service, Paola Pampaloni.

During this visit, the Maldives delegation will also meet with senior officials from Directorate-General for Trade (DG TRADE), Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA), Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (DG MARE), European External Action Service (EEAS), and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Belgium. The delegation will also meet with Members of the European Parliament and attend the opening of the Office of the Honorary Consul of the Maldives in Flanders, Belgium.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister of State Ahmed Khaleel congratulated the Ambassador on the presentation of credentials to the President, and expressed confidence that the bilateral ties between the Maldives and China will continue to prosper during her tenure.

State Minister conveyed his appreciation for the continuous support and assistance provided to the people of the Maldives by the Government of China, highlighting in particular the valuable support extended by the Government of China to the economic development of the Maldives.

Australian High Commissioner was accompanied to the ceremony by Second Secretary at the Australian High Commission Ms. Lara Sveinsson. en.title: The Classrooms Project in N. Lhohi and R. Kinolhas financed with Indian Grant Assistance inaugurated
en.description: The Classrooms Project in N. Lhohi and R. Kinolhas financed with Indian Grant Assistance inaugurated
en.body:
The Classrooms Project in N. Lhohi and R. Kinolhas financed with Indian Grant Assistance inaugurated

A virtual ceremony to mark the completion of the Classrooms Project in N. Lhohi School and R. Kinolhas School was held today. This project was funded with a combined grant of 12 million Rufiyaa, under the Indian Grant Assistance of 106 million Rufiyaa.

The Minister of Education Dr. Aishath Ali, Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, the High Commissioner of India to the Maldives Sunjay Sudhir delivered remarks at the event. The ceremony was also attended by the High Commissioner of Maldives to India Dr. Hussain Niyaaz, Secretary, Multilateral Dr. Hala Hameed and senior officials from the Ministry of Education and both schools.

Speaking at the event, Foreign Secretary Ghafoor highlighted the importance of implementing a holistic education system for the enhancement and overall enjoyment of school life for the students of Kinolhas School and Lhohi School. Under this project, additional classrooms have been constructed in both schools accommodating students in a single session of school, allowing schools to coordinate extra-curricular activities as a means to broadening perspectives of students and developing a diversity of skills and interests. Furthermore, the new classrooms provide access to advanced technology and increase accessibility by catering to the needs of differently abled students.

The financial support has been provided from the grant assistance of USD 6.9 million (MVR 106 million) granted to the Government of Maldives by the Government of India in March 2019. The aim of the grant assistance is to conduct socio-economic development projects across the country which are of high impact. The projects under this grant are managed by local authorities.

en.title: Japan provides a Grant Aid of 110Million Japanese Yen to the Maldives to the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship
en.description: Japan provides a Grant Aid of 110Million Japanese Yen to the Maldives to the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship
en.body:
Japan provides a Grant Aid of 110Million Japanese Yen to the Maldives to the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship

The Government of Japan provides a grant aid of 110 Million Japanese Yen (approximately USD 998,000) to the Maldives for the continuation of scholarship opportunities to be offered by the Government of Japan for the fiscal year 2022, under the Japanese Project for Human Resource Development (JDS).

The Minister of Higher Education, His Excellency Dr. Ibrahim Hassan and Resident Representative of Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) Mr. Mitsuyoshi Kawasaki signed the Agreement today at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Higher Education. Officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Higher Education, Embassy of Japan and JICA attended the ceremony.

On 15 July 2021, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid and the Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives, Her Excellency Keiko Yanai signed the Exchange of Notes relating to the grant aid, at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The grant will be utilised to provide fully funded scholarships for 6 Maldivian students again this year, a project which was implemented last year also by the Government of Japan for further promoting the Human Resource Development in the Maldives.

The Government of Japan has always been a consistent partner of the Maldives and has contributed to the development of social, environment, and education sectors in the Maldives.

dv.title: މުޅި ދިވެހި ގައުމު އޮތީ ޕެރަލިމްޕިކްސްގެ ދިވެހި އެތުލީޓުންނާއެކީ: ފޮރިންގ މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު
dv.description: މުޅި ދިވެހި ގައުމު އޮތީ ޕެރަލިމްޕިކްސްގެ ދިވެހި އެތުލީޓުންނާއެކީ: ފޮރިންގ މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު
dv.body:
މުޅި ދިވެހި ގައުމު އޮތީ ޕެރަލިމްޕިކްސްގެ ދިވެހި އެތުލީޓުންނާއެކީ: ފޮރިންގ މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު

މިއަހަރު ޖަޕާނުގައި ބާއްވާ ޕެރަލިމްޕިކްސްގައި ވާދަކުރުމަށްޓަކާ، ޖަޕާނުގައި މިވަގުތު ތިބި ދިވެހި އެތުލީޓުންނާއި، ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ އަބުދުﷲ ޝާހިދު ބައްދަލު ކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ. ޔޫއެންގެ ޖެނެރަލް އެސެމްބްލީގެ އިންތިޚާބީ ރައީސްގެ ހައިސިއްޔަތުން، ޖަޕާނު ސަރުކާރުގެ ދައުވަތަކަށް، މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު މިވަގުތު ހުންނެވީ ޖަޕާނުގައެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލު ކުރެއްވުމުގައި، ޕެރަލިމްޕިކްސްގައި ބައިވެރި ވުމަށް މިހާރު ޖަޕާނުގައި ތިބި ދިވެހި ޓީމުގެ ހުރިހާ ޑެލިގޭޓުންނާ ބައްދަލު ކުރައްވާ ދެއްކެވި ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ވިދާޅުވީ، މިއީ މި މުބާރާތުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ބައިވެރިވާ ފުރަތަމަ ފަހަރު ކަމަށްވުމާއެކު، މި މުބާރާތުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ތަމްސީލުކުރާ ހުރިހާ އެތުލީޓުންގެ ނަންވެސް ދިވެހި ތާރީޚުގައި ލިޔެވިގެންދާނެ ކަމާމެދު އެއްވެސް ޝައްކެއް ނުކުރައްވާ ކަމުގައެވެ. އަދި މި މުބާރާތުގައި ތަމްސީލުކުރާ ދިވެހި އެތުލީޓުން މުބާރާތުގައި ވާދަކުރުމަކީވެސް އޭގެ ޒާތުގައި ގައުމަށް ހޯއްދަވާ ދެއްވާ ރަން މެޑަލެއްކަމުގައި ވިދާޅުވެ މިނިސްޓަރ ވަނީ މި ދެ އެތުލީޓުންނާއި މުޅި ޑެލިގޭޝަނަށް މަރުޙަބާ ވިދާޅުވެ ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި ޚާއްޞަގޮތެއްގައި މާޒިންއާ ފާޠިމަތު އިބްރާހީމަކީ ވަރަށް އަޒުމާއި ހިތްވަރާއެކު ކުރިޔަށްދާ ދެ އެތުލީޓުންކަން ފާހަގަކުރައްވައި ދެ ބޭފުޅުންނަށް ވެސް ކާމިޔާބީއަށް އެދިވަޑައިގަން ނަވާފައިވެއެވެ. މިބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން މިނިސްޓަރ ވިދާޅުވެފައިވަނީ، ޕެރަލިމްޕިކްސް ދުވުމުގެ އިވެންޓުގައި ވާދަކުރާ ދިވެހި ދެ އެތުލީޓުން ކަމުގައިވާ މުޙައްމަދު މާޒިންއާ ފާޠިމަތު އިބްރާހީމު، ދުވުމުގެ ރޭހުގައި ވާދަކުރާ ދުވަހު، ދެ އެތުލީޓުންނަށް ހިއްވަރުދީ، އަދި ކާމިޔާބީއަށް އެދި ހެޔޮ ދުޢާކުރުމުގައި މުޅި ދިވެހި ގައުމުގެ ކުދިބޮޑު އެންމެހާ ރައްޔިތުންވެސް އެވަގުތު ދަނޑުގައި ލިބިކަމަށް ދެކެވަޑައިގެން، ހިތްވަރާއެކު، އިވެންޓުގައި ގައުމު ތަމްސީލުކޮށް ދިނުމަށް އެދިވަޑައިގަތެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި، އެތުލީޓުންނާއި އަދި ޓީމުގައި ހިމެނޭ އޮފިޝަލުން ދެއްކެވި ވާހަކާގައި، މި މުބާރަތަށް މަގުފަހި ކޮށްދިނުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ފޯރުކޮށްދިން އެހީތެރިކަމަށްޓަކާ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިބުރާހިމް މުހައްމަދު ސާލިހަށާއި އަދި ސަރުކާރަށް ޓީމުގެ ކުޅުންތެރިންނާއި އޮފިޝަލުންވަނީ ޝުކުރު އަދާކޮށްފައެވެ. އަދި ޔޫއެން ޖެނެރަލް އެސެމްބްލީގެ އިންތިޚާބީ ރައީސްގެ ހައިސިއްޔަތުން، ޖަޕާނަށް ކުރައްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި، ނުހަނު ބުރަކޮށް އުޅުއްވަމުންވެސް، ވަގުތު ހޯއްދަވައިގެން ކުޅުންތެރިންނާ އަދި އޮފިޝަލުންނާ ބައްދަލު ކުރެއްވި ކަމަށްޓަކާ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރަށްވެސް އެބޭފުޅުން ވަނީ ޝުކުރު އަދާކޮށްފައެވެ.

އަދި ޕެރަލިމްޕިކްސްގައި ވާދަކުރާ ކުޅުންތެރިންނާ އޮފިޝަލުންވަނީ، ޖަޕާނުގައި މި އިވެންޓުތައް ކުރިޔަށް ދާއިރު، އިންވެޓުތަކާގުޅޭ ޚަބަރުތައް، ވިހާވެސް ފުޅާ ދާއިރާއެއްގައި، ރާއްޖޭގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށާއި އަދި މުބާރާތުގައި ވާދަކުރާ ކުޅުންތެރިންގެ އާއިލާތަކާ ހަމައަށް ފޯރުކޮށް ދިނުމުގައި އެހީތެރިވެދިނުމަށް މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދުގެ ކިބައިން އެދިވަޑައިގެންފައެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދުވަނީ، މިމުބާރާތުގައި ރާއްޖެ ތަމްސީލުކުރާ ދެކުޅުންތެރިންނަށް، ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިބުރާހިމް މުހައްމަދު ސާލިހުގެ ފަރާތުން ތަހުނިޔާ އަރިސް ކޮށްފައެވެ. މިބައްދަކު ކުރެއްވުމުގައި، ޖާޕާނުގައި ހުންނަ ދިވެހި އެމްބެސެޑަރ އިބްރާހިމް އުވައިސްއާއި، ޑެޕިއުޓީ އެމްބެސެޑަރ މުހައްމަދު އަމީތުވެސް ބައިވެރިވެ ވަޑައިގަތެވެ.

ޖަޕާނުގައި ބާއްވާ ޕެރަލިމްޕިކް ގޭމްސްގައި މުޙައްމަދު މާޒިންއާއި ފާޠިމަތު އިބްރާހީމް ވާދަކުރުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައި ވަނީ 100 މީޓަރ ސްޕްރިންޓުގައެވެ.

en.title: Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Bahrain presents Credentials to the King of Bahrain
en.description: Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Bahrain presents Credentials to the King of Bahrain
en.body:
Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Bahrain presents Credentials to the King of Bahrain

The Non-Resident Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Maldives to the Kingdom of Bahrain, Mohamed Khaleel, presented his Letter of Credence to the King of Bahrain, His Majesty King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, at a ceremony held at Sakhir Palace, this evening.

During the ceremony, His Majesty the King congratulated the Ambassador on the commencement of his term, and conveyed greetings and best wishes to President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of Maldives. His Majesty the King also reaffirmed that the Government and the people of Bahrain would do their utmost to support the Ambassador during his term.

Following the Presentation of Credentials ceremony, Ambassador Khaleel attended a dinner hosted by the Undersecretary for Political Affairs, Dr. Shaikh Abdulla bin Ahmed bin Abdulla Al Khalifa. Ambassador Khaleel expressed his honour at being appointed the first Non-Resident Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to the Kingdom of Bahrain, and reaffirmed commitment to working closely together to enhance the existing ties of cooperation between the two countries.

The Ambassador was accompanied to the ceremony by the Minister-Counsellor of the Embassy of Maldives in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Badoora Saeed. The ceremony was attended by the Deputy Prime Minister of Bahrain, and other senior officials of the Government of the Kingdom of Bahrain.

en.title: Minister Shahid in his capacity as President-elect of the UN General Assembly to visit Japan
en.description: Minister Shahid in his capacity as President-elect of the UN General Assembly to visit Japan
en.body:
Minister Shahid in his capacity as President-elect of the UN General Assembly to visit Japan

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, in his capacity as the President-elect of the 76th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, at the invitation of the Government of Japan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Japan from 26-28 August 2021.

During the visit, Minister Shahid will make a courtesy call on Hon. Suga Yoshihide, Prime Minister of Japan, and will also meet with Hon. Motegi Toshimitsu, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan.

The visit will provide an opportunity for both the Minister, in his capacity as the President-elect, and the Government of Japan to hold close consultations on enhancing cooperation within the auspices of the United Nations General Assembly. The visit will also focus on bilateral aspects of the relationship between Maldives and Japan.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Ukraine
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Ukraine
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Ukraine

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends message of felicitations to Dmytro Kuleba, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Ukraine.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and best wishes to Your Excellency, and the people of Ukraine, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Ukraine.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress of the people of Ukraine and the assurances of my highest considerations.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka
en.description: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message expressing condolences to Professor Gamini Lakshman Peiris, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, following the death of His Excellency Mangala Samaraweera, Former Foreign Minister of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It was with deep sorrow that I learned of the untimely demise of the former Foreign Minister, His Excellency Mangala Samaraweera. He will be remembered for his long and distinguished service to the Government and people of Sri Lanka. His contribution to promote Maldives-Sri Lanka bilateral relations are also greatly appreciated.

At this time of profound sadness, the Government and the people of the Maldives join me in extending our condolences and prayers to his family, the Government and people of Sri Lanka.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration”.

en.title: Japan donates 112,000 doses AstraZeneca vaccines to the Maldives through COVAX
en.description: Japan donates 112,000 doses AstraZeneca vaccines to the Maldives through COVAX
en.body:
Japan donates 112,000 doses AstraZeneca vaccines to the Maldives through COVAX

Japan has donated 112,000 doses of the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccines to the Maldives through the WHO Covax Facility, as part of Japan’s “Last One Mile Support” initiative. His Excellency Ahmed Naseem, Minister of Health, received the vaccines on behalf of the Government of Maldives at a ceremony held today at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Speaking at the ceremony, Minister Naseem thanked the Government of Japan for their generous donations, not only in providing the vaccines but also in donating medical equipment, medical supplies and other assistance given to the Maldives and the Maldivian people throughout the pandemic. He mentioned that this donation of AstraZeneca vaccines will contribute towards the Government’s efforts to continue vaccination across the country and will support the goal of completing the vaccination programme for the entire eligible population.

Her Excellency Keiko Yanai, Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives also spoke at the ceremony and highlighted the friendly and historic ties between the two countries. She mentioned that Maldives is an important bilateral partner of Japan, and reiterated its continued support to the Maldives during its times of need.

This donation is the fourth COVAX allocation to the Maldives. Earlier in August, the United States donated 128,700 doses of Pfizer vaccines through the WHO Covax Faculity which are being administered presently.

Today’s ceremony was also attended by His Excellency Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, Foreign Secretary, Ms. Catherine Haswell, UN Resident Coordinator, Ms. Marjan Montazemi, UNICEF Country Representative along with senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Health, Maldives National Defence Force, Embassy of Japan in Maldives, and WHO Maldives.

dv.title: ޖަޕާން ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް އެސްޓްރާޒެނެކާ ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފި
dv.description: ޖަޕާން ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް އެސްޓްރާޒެނެކާ ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފި

ޖަޕާން ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް އެސްޓްރާޒެނެކާ ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފި

ކޮވެކްސް ފެސިލިޓީ މެދުވެރިކޮށް، ޖަޕާން ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް 112،000 (އެއްލައްކަ ބާރަ ހާސް) ޑޯޒްގެ އެސްޓްރާޒެނެކާ ކޮވިޑް-19 ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފިއެވެ. މި ވެކްސިން ހަދިޔާކޮށްފައިވަނީ ޖަޕާންގެ "ލާސްޓް ވަން މައިލް ސަޕޯޓް"ގެ ދަށުންނެވެ. މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއަރޒްގައި މިއަދު ހެނދުނު އޮތް ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ވެކްސިންއާ ހަވާލުވެވަޑައިގަތީ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ހެލްތު، އަހުމަދު ނަސީމް އެވެ. މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން ހެލްތު މިނިސްޓަރ ނަސީމް ވަނީ ޖަޕާން ސަރުކާރުން ވެދެއްވި ދީލަތި އެހީއަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި ވެކްސިންގެ އިތުރުން، ކޮވިޑް-19ގެ ބަލިމަޑުކަމުގައި މެޑިކަލް އިކުއިޕްމަންޓް އާއި މެޑިކަލް ސަޕްލައިގެ އިތުރުން ޖަޕާން ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރަށް ފޯރުކޮށްދީފައިވާ އެހެނިހެން ދީލަތި އެހީތަކަށް މިނިސްޓަރ ނަސީމް ވަނީ ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާފައެވެ. ޖަޕާނުން މި ފޯރުކޮށްދިން ވެކްސިންއާއެކު، ރާއްޖޭގެ މުޅި އާބާދީއަށް ވެކްސިން ދިނުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ހިފާފައިވާ އަމާޒަށް ވާސިލްވުމަށް އިތުރަށް ފަސޭހަ ވެގެންދާނެކަންވެސް މިނިސްޓަރ ނަސީމް ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ. ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން ޖަޕާނުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު ކެއިކޯ ޔަނާއީ ވަނީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާ ޖަޕާނާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގާތް ގުޅުމަށް އަލިއަޅުއްވާލައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ބޭނުމެއް ޖެހިއްޖެ ކޮންމެ ހިނދެއްގައިވެސް ޖަޕާނުން އެހީތެރިކަން ފޯރުކޮށްދޭނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން އެކަމަނާ ދެއްވިއެވެ. މިއަދު ރާއްޖެއަށް ލިބުނު ވެކްސިން ޝިޕްމަންޓަކީ ދުނިޔޭގެ ސިއްހަތު ޖަމްއިއްޔާ (ޑަބްލިޔު.އެޗް.އޯ)ގެ ކޮވެކްސް ފެސިލިޓީ މެދުވެރިކޮށް ރާއްޖެއަށް ލިބުނު ވެކްސިންގެ 4 ވަނަ ޝިޕްމަންޓެވެ. ކޮވެކްސްގެ ދަށުން މި އޮގަސްޓްމަހުގެ ކުރީކޮޅު އެމެރިކާއިން ފޯރުކޮށްދިން 128،700 ޑޯޒްގެ ފައިޒާ ވެކްސިން ލިބި، މިހާރު ދަނީ ވެކްސިން ޖަހަމުންނެވެ. ޖަޕާނުން ހަދިޔާކުރި ވެކްސިން ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާ ހަވާލުކުރުމަށް މިއަދު ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި، ފޮރިން ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޢަބްދުލް ޣަފޫރު މުޙައްމަދު، އދ އިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ރެޒިޑެންޓް ކޯޑިނޭޓަރ ކެތެރިން ހެސްވެލް، ޔުނިސެފް ކަންޓްރީ ރެޕްރެޒެންޓޭޓިވް މަރްޖާން މޮންތަޒޭމީގެ އިތުރުން މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއަރޒްއާއި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ހެލްތުގެ އިސް ބޭފުޅުންނާއި، ޑަބްލިޔު.އެޗް.އޯ، އެމް.އެން.ޑީ.އެފް އަދި މާލޭގައި ހުންނަ ޖަޕާން އެމްބަސީގެ އިސް އޮފިޝަލުން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތެވެ.
